description:
Hi! I’m Albert, a Computer Science and Software Engineering student from Côte d’Ivoire with a strong interest in AI, software, data, and technology for social impact.

I enjoy turning ideas into practical solutions. I have experience with machine learning, data analysis, web and mobile development, and I’ve worked on projects involving healthcare, agriculture, IoT, and digital solutions for local communities. I also enjoy teamwork, problem-solving, and taking initiative when working.
summary:
FORBITS is a bilingual (French and English) interactive storytelling website designed to help students aged 11 to 15 discover the technology NASA has left behind on the Moon and Mars, and understand the science we have learned from it.

Each chapter focuses on one piece of equipment, such as the Apollo Lunar Module or the Opportunity rover. In just a few short screens, students follow its story, discover one important scientific idea supported by a NASA source, answer a short quiz, and then connect what they have learned to something familiar through a “Back home” section. For example, students in Côte d’Ivoire can relate Martian dust affecting Opportunity to the harmattan dust that settles on solar panels at home.

The experience also changes with each world: warm rust tones for Mars and cool blue tones for the Moon. More importantly, FORBITS is designed for the reality of its users. It is lightweight, works on low-end phones and slow internet connections, and does not require an account.

The goal is simple: turn forgotten machines on other worlds into stories that young students can understand, remember, and connect to their own lives. Every scientific fact is supported by a source from nasa.gov.
details:
WHAT IT DOES

FORBITS turns NASA's left-behind hardware into a guided story. A student follows the same path every time:

1. Welcome. Sankofa, the robot guide, greets the student and offers French or English.

2. Choose a world. The Moon, Mars, or Beyond (asteroids and deep space).

3. Arrive. A rocket launches, travels and lands. The student explores a 3D globe made from NASA Moon (LRO) and Mars (Viking) maps, where each machine sits at its real coordinates. A "time machine" slider shows what was there in each year since 1966.

4. Meet a machine. The machine introduces itself in its own voice ("I was built to last 90 sols. I lasted 5,111.") and tells its mission in six steps: design, launch, arrival, exploration, discovery, legacy.

5. From part to discovery. As the story goes on, the camera moves to the part of the NASA 3D model that made each discovery possible (a solar panel, a wheel, a laser reflector), with a NASA source.

6. Try it. Short experiments: time a laser echo from the Moon, fly Ingenuity in thin Martian air, keep Opportunity's solar panels clean.

7. Prove it. A quiz, with an explanation after each answer, unlocks the machine's collectible card.

An Explorer mode lets students drive a small rover and replay the real paths of Perseverance, Curiosity and Ingenuity, sol by sol, from NASA/JPL data. A Sources page lists every reference, machine by machine.

The 13 machines: Surveyor 3, Apollo 11 Eagle, Apollo 15 Lunar Roving Vehicle, Apollo 15 laser retroreflector (Moon); Viking 1, Sojourner, Opportunity, InSight, Ingenuity, Curiosity, Perseverance (Mars); NEAR Shoemaker, Pioneer 10 (Beyond).

HOW IT WORKS

- Front end: React and TypeScript (Vite), Three.js with React Three Fiber for 3D, GSAP for animation, i18next for French/English, installable as a PWA.

- Back end: a Django REST API holds all content (stories, dates, quizzes, sources, voices) in both languages. Its admin panel lets non-developers on the team write and correct stories without touching code.

- 3D: official NASA 3D Resources models, reduced by the team to load on mid-range phones, and Moon figures the team built from NASA mission report dimensions.

- Data: rover paths converted from NASA/JPL MMGIS GeoJSON files by a small Python script.

- Voices: each machine's narration is generated in advance from our own texts with ElevenLabs (AI voice generation, see AI disclosure below). Every spoken line is also shown as text.

- Hosting: Docker Compose with Caddy (HTTPS). Source code: https://github.com/E-hackaton/space

BENEFITS

- Science made simple: each machine is explained in plain words, linked to one discovery it made possible.

- French first: most space content online is in English; FORBITS treats French as a first-class language.

- Mobile first: works in a phone browser, no installation, no account.

- Accessible: subtitles for every voice line, reduced-motion support, adjustable quality settings for weaker phones, quiz feedback given in words and not only by colour.

- Safe for minors: no account, no personal data collected; progress stays on the student's own device.

- Scientifically checked: every date, number and location is tied to a NASA source shown on the page.

WHAT WE HOPE TO ACHIEVE

Most students in Côte d'Ivoire rarely meet the history of space exploration in their own language. We want FORBITS used in secondary-school classrooms and shared by teachers and students over WhatsApp. Our first goal is a pilot with [2 classes / 1 school] in Abidjan during the 2026–2027 school year, with [partner]. We will measure success simply: how many students finish a chapter and choose to start another, collected through teacher feedback and a short paper questionnaire in class.

WHAT MAKES IT CREATIVE

A story, not a museum: each machine speaks in the first person. "From part to discovery": every story ties one piece of engineering to what it made possible. Sankofa, an Akan symbol meaning "go back and fetch what was left behind", sums up the challenge and roots it in Côte d'Ivoire. Learning by doing: the experiments turn a fact into a gesture.

AI DISCLOSURE

- Claude (Anthropic), large language model: coding assistant (React, Django, 3D scenes), first drafts of texts and of the demo video edit. Every text was reviewed by the team and every fact checked against NASA sources.

- ElevenLabs, voice generation: the guide and the 13 machines are voiced from scripts written by the team, with adult premade voices; no real person's voice was cloned. Audio files carry this notice in their metadata.

- No AI-generated images. No NASA logo, flag, insignia or mission identifier was generated, used or modified.

TOOLS

React, TypeScript, Vite, Three.js, React Three Fiber, drei, GSAP, Tailwind CSS, Zustand, i18next, vite-plugin-pwa, Django, Django REST Framework, Python, Blender, Docker, Caddy, ElevenLabs, Claude by Anthropic, ffmpeg and HyperFrames.

TEAM

COULIBALY NAHOUO ALBERT - Project lead, pitch and video

COULIBALY SEYDOU — Back end (Django API, deployment)

ALLOMA JEAN LUC — Front end and 3D (React, Three.js, 3D)

DIARRASSOUBA DJAMILAT - Storytelling and quizzes

FOFANA ISSOUF - Business and marketing
dataRefs: NSSDCA Master Catalog - one record per machine (Surveyor 3, Apollo 11 Eagle, Apollo 15 LM/LRV/LRRR, Viking 1, Opportunity, Curiosity, InSight, Perseverance/Ingenuity, NEAR Shoemaker, Pioneer 10)
NASA NTRS - Apollo 15 Preliminary Science Report SP-289, laser ranging retroreflector
NASA SVS - CGI Moon Kit (LRO LROC colour, LOLA relief) and Blue Marble Next Generation (Earth)
NASA Science mission pages - Surveyor 3, Viking 1, Mars Pathfinder, Spirit & Opportunity, InSight, Curiosity, Perseverance, Ingenuity, NEAR Shoemaker, Pioneer 10
projectRefs: USGS Astrogeology - Mars Viking MDIM 2.1 colour mosaic (NASA/JPL/USGS, public domain)
Open-source software - React, Three.js, React Three Fiber, GSAP, Tailwind, i18next, Django, Django REST Framework, Caddy; fonts Fira Sans and Overpass (SIL OFL); Phosphor Icons (MIT)
AI tools - Claude by Anthropic (code and drafting), ElevenLabs (voices from team scripts)
Team-made - Venus and Saturn illustrations (not real maps), Web Audio sound effects, Sankofa character, Moon 3D figures from NASA mission report dimensions
ElevenLabs - AI voice generation for the guide and the 13 machines, from scripts written by the team (adult premade voices, no cloned voice)
